text:
maria_se: Heads up — FinServ POC asking for hybrid setup. They want our Private deployment reachable from their on‑prem via PrivateLink (interface endpoint) + an onprem TLS inspection device. Key asks: preserve client source IP for logging, mTLS from their proxy to our endpoint, and support long‑lived streaming sockets (pin connections). Also need a minimal firewall allowlist (incl NTP/OCSP). cc @james_sales

james_sales: thanks. customer is AWS (not GovCloud), enterprise bank, SOC2 + some Fed controls. timeline: POC next week. Any immediate blockers?

maria_se: they NAT outgoing to one or two egress IPs, but TLS inspection re‑terminates TLS — they said they can create an allowlist on the inspection box. They prefer not to run an extra reverse proxy if avoidable.

rachel_neteng: quick summary from networking side: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) will terminate at an ENI in the VPC — the source IP seen on our service will be the ENI IP (i.e., not the original onprem client IP). If preserving the original client IP is mandatory, options are: 1) have their proxy forward original IP in X-Forwarded-For (or a custom header) over TLS; 2) use a TCP proxy in their VPC that terminates the original client traffic and forwards with preserved src ip inside the VPC (more complex); 3) uplift to a dedicated Private deployment with a customer egress appliance (we can discuss).

rachel_neteng: for mTLS: we do support mutual TLS for Private deployments. For Hosted+PrivateLink we can accept client certs on our endpoint but we need to exchange CA bundle details beforehand. Security team will want cert rotation cadence.
achel_neteng: about streaming sockets: our default gateway idle timeout is ~15m for HTTP/1.1 streaming. For HTTP/2 / gRPC we maintain longer active streams; recommend HTTP/2 or WebSocket+ping for pinning. If they need >15m idle we can request an increase for Dedicated or Private installs.

navin_ops: firewall allowlist snippet — customer can restrict egress to these: 

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood Private endpoint (example)
- DEST_CIDR: 10.22.3.0/26    # interface endpoint ENI range (example)
- PORTS: tcp/443

# Auxiliary services needed from onprem to our infra
- OCSP: tcp/80, tcp/443 to vendor OCSP endpoints (or allow egress to our OCSP proxy)
- NTP: udp/123 (time sync)
- DNS: udp/53 (if they use external DNS); for PrivateLink we recommend VPC private hosted zone so DNS stays internal
```

navin_ops: note: replace DEST_CIDR with the ENI CIDRs we give you. If they NAT all outbound to a single public IP, allowlist the public egress IPs and 443.

ben_sales: any cost delta we should flag for the customer? e.g., data processing on PrivateLink, Dedicated platform fees, or special config charges?

rachel_neteng: yes — AWS charges for data processed through interface endpoints. On our side: Hosted + PrivateLink = standard per‑token usage pricing + any PrivateLink setup assistance. Dedicated/Private deployment = platform fee + committed capacity pricing; longer idle stream support and cert integration are typically part of Dedicated/Private SOW. I'll flag estimated network egress costs in the handoff.

maria_se: security questionnaire items they asked: cert rotation policy, HSM/KMS support for keys, audit log retention, and whether we can provide network diagrams. Who owns answers?

security-bot: @maria_se For formal questionnaire: send to security@redwood.com with the doc attached. We support KMS/HSM for Private deployments, audit logging with configurable retention, and cert rotation guidance. We can provide redacted network diagrams and architecture blobs for POC.

rachel_neteng: action items:
- I will generate a one‑page allowlist with exact ENI CIDRs + ports and a short note on DNS split‑horizon (deliverable: doc + example bind/Route53 entries).
- @navin_ops will confirm stream idle timeout and provide recommended HTTP/2 keepalive config.
- @ben_sales please collect POC egress public IP(s) and whether TLS inspection can forward XFF header.
- @maria_se schedule 30m tech sync with customer and include security@redwood.com.

maria_se: thanks — will set up. For the allowlist doc please include this quick snippet for their TLS inspection team to copy/paste. :thumbsup:

rachel_neteng: example keepalive for gRPC (suggested):
```
# gRPC keepalive settings (client)
keepalive_time = 30s
keepalive_timeout = 10s
permit_without_stream = true
```

navin_ops: FYI internal note: if customer insists on raw src IP preservation we need to scope a VPC transit appliance or a proxy hop in their VPC; plan for ~2 day effort for network validation in POC.

ben_sales: noted — I'll surface that as an optional engineering work item for the SOW.

maria_se: perfect. landing this for now — tech sync invites incoming.
